title: Kushinagar, traditional place of the Buddha's death
summary: Town in eastern Uttar Pradesh that Buddhist tradition names as the place where the Buddha died among the Mallas. The ruins include a main stupa and a Nirvana temple with a 6.1 m reclining sandstone Buddha, originally installed in the 5th century CE, and the Ramabhar cremation stupa.

uncertainty.note: The Buddha's death date is traditional and debated; the monuments run from the earlier centuries CE (the statue is 5th century CE per the Indian government's UNESCO tentative-list text). End is the present.

as_recorded.value: the Buddha tells Ananda to go to Kusinara, where he dies
Nirvana statue originally installed in the fifth century A.D.

when.display: Traditional site of the Buddha's death (c. 5th century BCE, debated); monuments to the 5th century CE and later

where.modern_name: Kushinagar (Kasia), Kushinagar district, Uttar Pradesh, India

importance.justification: One of the four principal Buddhist pilgrimage places, marking the Buddha's death in tradition.

sources.title: Maha-parinibbana Sutta: Last Days of the Buddha (DN 16), translated by Sister Vajira and Francis Story
Silk Road Sites in India (Tentative List no. 5492): Buddhist Remains of Kushinagar
sources.publisher: UNESCO World Heritage Centre (text by Government of India)

reviewer_note: The sutta source is a translation of the canonical text and is undated; the death date is traditional. The Indian tentative-list entry gives 26 45 N, 83 55 E (to the arcminute), while Wikidata gives 26.740 N, 83.889 E, so uncertainty is set to 3 km. I found no model-quality dimensions: the tentative text says the main stupa may once have reached 45.72 m but gives no plan dimension. Confidence "probable" because the schema has no "traditional" level.
